title: Promise states and chaining
learningObjectives: Explain promise states and chaining and implement reliable browser event and network workflows.

understand.concept: A Promise begins pending and settles once as fulfilled or rejected. then() returns a new Promise; returned values fulfil the next stage, returned promises are adopted, and thrown errors reject the next stage.
understand.whyItMatters: Promise chaining composes asynchronous operations and propagates errors. Missing return statements can cause later stages to run before nested work completes.
understand.analogy: Each promise stage passes a value or failure to the next stage.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy is simplified; JavaScript scheduling, HTTP semantics, and browser security follow platform standards.

explain.narrative: The first handler returns 8; the next throws, so the chain reaches catch.

examples.explanation: The first handler returns 8; the next throws, so the chain reaches catch.
examples.expectedOutput: Console or UI output demonstrates the concept; network examples require a configured endpoint.

practise.guidedTask: Create a three-stage chain and intentionally reject in the middle. Trace the value and error path.
practise.independentTask: Build an asynchronous feature with explicit states, cancellation, and error handling. Document which failures are safe to retry.
hints: Separate HTTP errors from network and parsing errors.
Use bounded retries only for suitable operations.
Tie UI updates to the latest active request.

questions.explanation: then returns a new promise that adopts the handler result or thrown error.

options: Model loading, empty, success, failure, and cancellation states
